_comment: WorldBench V5 SCENE DEFINITION — planet generation's fifth generation (resonance fields), beside Populous (V4), which it does not touch. Same bench frame: window stack → paged_menu (page rail + per-page tab rail) → panel | RTT | panel → nav footer. The behaviour (`worldbench`) parses this tree once, worldbench.lua's arrange() lights the selected slice, the globe draws in the centre pane.

children._comment: One tab per FIELD with controls; each option's `enabled_bind` is its field's tab-enabled key published from the FIELDS tree.

THE RESONANCE STACK: the stack's dials (spread = how far a slot's heard height strays from its dial in octaves, seam = the seam ribbon's half-width in tiles from a converging plate edge, mask seed) and its re-roll above; below, one row per SLOT — ON · f (cycles per great circle) · a (its own height, percent of radius) · w (sinusoids in the train) · how its alpha mask is CUT: none, by AREA (the mask wave's blotches) or along the SEAM (the plate scheme's CONVERGING edges under the heat's push — where the plates are shoved together, the layer LIFTS as a range; PLATES, WARP and REROLL PLATES on the Epochs tab and RANDOMIZE SEAMS on the Heat tab all move them). The opening rows are the engine's layers: continents, seabeds, shelves, mountains, foothills, hills — and UNDER THE HEX the same layers finer (256 to 49152 cycles), which the hex grid does not carry and the 2K hex evaluates exactly: one list, one algorithm, two resolutions.

THE EPOCHS — the stone ocean moving: the land masses the waves made are rigid RAFTS, the floor flows with the heat's push (which breathes over the epochs); floor crowding goes under (UPLIFT = the isostatic share that stands up), two rafts crowding weld, a raft the push tears at RIFTs; RATE = tiles the fastest crust moves per tick (hundredths); IMPACTS = strikes a thousand epochs (radii a power law, most small, a few vast — crater waves on the crust); hot vents erupt DROPS as the push breathes; the RUN box (how many epochs RUN plays, across frames; RUN again pauses), TICK one epoch, RESET to the composed world.
VIEW — what the globe shows on this tab: the RELIEF, or the HARDNESS ledger every parcel carries (soft → hard, the `hardness` style block), as the epochs move and thicken it.

THE EROSION — the era (water, air, weathering: Evolution's surface procedures) ADOPTED over the world before it, the epoched planet with its hardness ledger: the RUN box (surface cycles RUN plays across frames; RUN again pauses), TICK one cycle, RESET to the world before; the LOOP box runs THE FOREVER LOOP (write back, move, adopt, cut). The cut is hardness-selective; the relief's texture is the readout to watch.

THE FOREVER LOOP — each step writes the era's cut back into the crust's parcels, moves LOOP_EPOCHS epochs (compression, drops, strikes over the eroded world), adopts the moved world anew and cuts LOOP_CYCLES cycles; the box counts steps, LOOP plays them across frames (LOOP again pauses).

THE TILE — MATERIALIZE the hex the camera faces at 2K (the one recipe's fields evaluated exactly at every pixel — the layers under the hex, the bubbles' every octave — a fine expression of the same algorithm) on its own thread; the picture replaces the globe in the centre pane while this tab is selected.

THE WATER — CUT: passes of rain the pixel eroder runs over the materialized hex (rain gathers downhill, cuts by the hex's hardness read at every pixel, carries, settles; nothing under the sea line); 0 leaves the fields' ground as made. Read at the next MATERIALIZE.
VIEW — what the centre pane shows of the materialized hex: its PICTURE (the 2K map hill-shaded), or its FIELD (the hex as the engine's quad field, flown over).

THE MATERIALIZER's controls (the UX law: a click PICKS; a control does what it says). RENDER HEX materializes the picked hex (with the TILE tab's CUT) on the tile thread, ahead of everything, and draws it in the world when it lands — shown while a hex is picked and the materializer rests. RENDER WORLD walks every hex not yet drawn, nearest the picked hex first — shown while the materializer rests. STOP halts it: the hex in flight dropped back on the queue, the walk paused (RENDER WORLD resumes it) — shown while it runs. The ultimate render is every hex of the world — a long job the sheet shows filling in.

THE MAP page's sheet — the world laid flat through the shared WorldMap (contract FF8A575D): drag pans, wheel zooms to a hex, a click PICKS a hex — outlined on the sheet in the stage's third shell ink, nothing rendered; RENDER HEX materializes it (with the TILE tab's CUT) and draws it IN THE WORLD on its cell; RENDER WORLD walks every hex. Seated only while this page is lit.

THE FIELD — the materialized hex as the engine's quad field: one 128 ft quad per pixel of the mask at its LOD8 vector (the pixel's composite, the heightmap as it is), wearing the tile's picture, the drops between neighbours drawn as walls; flown over with the orbit camera (drag orbits, right-drag pans across the ground, wheel zooms from the whole hex to one quad). Shown while the TILE tab's VIEW says FIELD and a field has been built.

THE TILE — the hex the camera faces, materialized at 2K through the pixel tier (flicker-worldtile) over the world as it stands; the picture is the tile's own hill-shaded map, uploaded as HUD texture 3 (after the theme's three). Shown instead of the globe while the TILE tab is selected and a hex has been materialized; a missing image draws nothing.

THE FIELD TREE (indent = child, which inherits its parent's enable): WAVE › mask · RESONANCE (the whole stack; its slots switch on the Resonance tab) · HEAT › EMITTERS · BUBBLES (domes and bowls at every scale, the rounded field kind beside the trains: the octaves the hex grid resolves on the globe, every octave at the tile) · EPOCHS (the motion, compression and compaction ticked over the composed world; off, the composed world stands) · EROSION (the era over the world before it).
THE HEX IN FLIGHT: which hex the materializer is cutting and the passes run of its cut, and the same as a gauge — the per-hex progress the MAP page owes (incident C666ADAC).

worldbench_map._comment: THE MAP's stage (WorldMap contract FF8A575D) — the WorldBench's world laid flat. Same authored vocabulary as the bench's globe: the FIRST shell colour is the sheet's backdrop ink, the SECOND the tile base (inset 0 on the flat sheet), the THIRD the ink the picked hex is outlined in (the nav contract's gold rim), the graticule layer the shared reference frame drawn flat. The cells are painted emissive (data ink reads exactly) and the hexes' 2K pictures are laid over them; same HDR resolve as the globe so the views agree.

worldbench_field._comment: THE FIELD's stage — the materialized hex as the engine's quad field (flicker_voxel::QuadField): the bench publishes the field's region meshes as the scene's `shells` (one 128 ft quad per pixel at its LOD8 vector, the drops between neighbours as walls, flat-shaded from each face's own geometry, wearing the tile's picture) and the orbit camera flies over them, so NO `camera` block and no authored shell: `clear` transparent so the holder panel shows through, the same studio light and the same HDR resolve as the globe so the two views agree.

worldbench_globe._comment: The WORLDBENCH V5 globe — the hex world drawn into the centre viewport, same authored vocabulary as the Populous globe: NO `camera` block (the scene's orbit camera owns the view), `clear` transparent so the holder panel shows through, the near-black under-shell and the inset tile shell over it (the seams between tiles ARE the outlines), the shared reference frame above both. The bench EXTRUDES both shells per cell by the wave's relief and tints the tile shell by the `wave` style block; the radii, insets and static colours stay authored here.
worldbench_globe._hdr: HDR: the `scene` pass (the globe's two shells + graticule, the layers above) renders into the LINEAR rgba16f `hdr` working attachment and `tonemap_grade` resolves it (ACES roll-off) into the sRGB `color` last. grade_strength 0 = tonemap only, no invented tint — an art grade is Aaron's to author in-window. Alpha passes through, so the transparent clear the holder panel shows through survives.

nav_footer._comment: Bench nav rail band (the materialbench/catalog block, same values). `frame` = the node's own slab; `rule` (top hairline) + `label` (legend ink) resolve as the component's defaults.
nav_footer.label: $dim

rtt_holder._comment: The framed RTT HOLDER every bench's rtt/viewport slot styles against — the shared chrome for an offscreen-view slot (replaced the per-scene meshbench holder block, same values).

load._comment: The bootstrap-roll progress bar reuses the loading-screen gauge look (same values as Loading.scene.json load.gauge); per-scene styles by design, palette tokens single-sourced in ui_theme.json.

wave._comment: The SEA sphere's ink (five-line split: palette tokens here, numbers to the Rust): `sea` its colour, `sea_alpha` its blend, `sea_gloss` its wet sheen. The tile shell's tint is the `relief` block.

relief._comment: THE RELIEF RAMP the tile shell is tinted by, against the SEA and the shape's own floor and summit (the engine's `Ramp`, the same one the evaluator's flat maps use): `deep`→`shallow` below the waterline by depth, `lowland`→`upland`→`summit` above it by height.

hardness._comment: THE HARDNESS LEDGER's two stops, the epochs tab's HARDNESS view: `soft` sediment and weathered hills → `hard` orogenic belts, basalt floor and metamorphic root.

field._comment: The RUN box — the shared text field's ink in the bench's palette.
field.label: $ink
